title: Windows signing: which route
context: Your question: "can I go to my windows, and sign there?" Yes. The build stays here; you copy the finished installer and portable exe to your Windows PC, sign them there with Microsoft's signtool, and copy them back. You still need a certificate from a seller: only that quiets SmartScreen, and since 2023 its key must sit on a USB card or a cloud service. On Windows, Certum becomes an option: its cloud certificate (SimplySign) is a Windows app that acts as a card reader, which had no Linux route here. Resellers list it at about 116 USD a year on a 3-year term; Certum's own shop sells a set with a physical card from 379 EUR. Whether Certum issues the Standard certificate to an individual in Norway, and the exact 2026 price, I check before you buy.

You chose to sign the Windows build. The options are in docs/desktop-release.md (Windows signing). The cheapest and simplest to run from this Linux machine is Microsoft's Azure Artifact Signing at about 10 USD a month, but Microsoft only accepts individuals in the USA and Canada. From Norway it needs an organisation, so you'd register a sole proprietorship (enkeltpersonforetak) at Brreg, with a website and an email on its domain. Whether Microsoft accepts a sole proprietorship hasn't been confirmed. Validation takes 1 to 20 business days.

Without a company: SSL.com validates individuals, at about 180 USD a year for its cloud signing plus a certificate fee that isn't clear from their site. Signing from Linux with it is likely but not yet tested.
Either way, SmartScreen warnings fade gradually as more people install the game. Even the expensive EV certificates no longer skip that.
Read the provider's terms of use before paying. The agent couldn't open them, so it's not confirmed what they say about game content.
question: Which signing route should we take, now that signing on your Windows PC is an option?

options.label: certum-windows
options.note: Certum Standard code signing (SimplySign cloud, or the physical card set) as an individual, signed on your Windows PC with signtool. I confirm individual eligibility and price first, and write the copy-sign-copy steps.

options.label: azure-company
options.note: Register a sole proprietorship and use Azure Artifact Signing, about 120 USD a year. You do the registration, the Azure account and the ID check; I wire the signing into the build.

options.label: sslcom-individual
options.note: SSL.com as an individual, no company, about 180 USD a year plus the certificate. I test the Linux signing first, before you pay.

options.label: later
options.note: Ship unsigned for now and decide on signing when a release is close.
